newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes slightly easier in quiet Asian market.
newsitem.headline: Crudes slightly easier in quiet Asian market.

text.p: Crude oil prices dipped modestly in the Asian market on Thursday in quiet trading marked by an absence of many traders due to a public holiday, market participants said.
Traders in many countries in Asia, including Singapore and South Korea, were away for the Labour Day holiday.

June cash Brent was notionally assessed at $18.40/18.50 per barrel at 0840 GMT, down five cents from late Wednesday U.S levels. SIMEX Brent futures remained unchanged, with the June contract bid/offered at $18.43/18.50, compared with the IPE close of $18.52 on Wednesday.
In the physical market for Gulf crudes, at least four June Oman cargoes appeared to be available in the market.

Traders were mixed on whether there was much buying interest in the medium grade crude. A U.S. major and China, which often buys Oman, did not appear to be showing much appetite for the crude, some traders said.
In regional crudes, China was believed to have purchased Indonesian Minas crude from a Japanese trader and a western trader. Details could not be confirmed, however.
